map_identity_conflicts.evidence: The two independent construction functions each call the receiver-returning MapObjActor constructor and unconditionally install different primary address points at receiver offset zero. The Seagull function has no control-flow branch and no call after its final primary installation. Native disassembly confirms both store instructions. The Seagull registry spelling does not prove the original C++ class spelling.
map_identity_conflicts.packet_annotation_requirement: Do not label every word of this map row RailDot or Seagull. Use an independently established table/address-point region; preserve unresolved ownership at a boundary.

confidence_and_limits: High confidence means the owned EU binary directly connects a registry creator, its construction function, the receiver and the recorded primary installation.
An accepted C++ name records current source/map identity only. Registry spelling alone does not prove an original C++ class spelling.
Historical candidate links are retained for faithful recovery. Only actor candidates separately confirmed by the corrected trace receive the independent verification flag.
GeneratorBox, GhostPlayer and Gorori have internal branches after their unconditional primary installations. No alternate direct primary installation appears in their constructor bodies.

BlockRailTerminater, CoinGathering and NoteObj have later calls while the analysis still tracks the original receiver in r0. These calls are recorded; the scan does not claim a full recursive final-state proof for them.
Complete vtable group boundaries, all secondary vptr identities, class layouts, virtual signatures, and method ownership are outside this scan.
The RailDot map row also contains the separately established Seagull primary address point. No map name or boundary is changed by this proposal.

packet_annotation_guidance.preferred_lookup: Use a verified primary address point or a verified table region and its registry name. Treat registry_name as an actor identifier. Show an accepted_cpp_class_name separately when supplied.
packet_annotation_guidance.shared_targets: A function can be referenced by multiple tables through inheritance. Record every referencing table; do not infer one method owner from the table label.
packet_annotation_guidance.slot_numbering: Existing factory slot numbers are raw word indices relative to the recorded map row. Preserve that convention explicitly unless a separate ABI slot normalization is proved.
packet_annotation_guidance.interior_address_points: A map row can include more than one primary table. The RailDot/Seagull conflict must remain unresolved for whole-row annotation until the actual referenced region is identified.
packet_annotation_guidance.exact_lookup: packet_lookup_by_primary_address_point is keyed only by the exact address stored into the actor object. It does not accept a containing map-row start, an arbitrary slot address or a secondary address point as a substitute.
packet_annotation_guidance.original_class_names: original_cpp_class_name is null throughout. An accepted_cpp_class_name is a separately evidenced current project identity, not a claim that a registry spelling or broad map-row name proves the original C++ spelling.
